Jazz is a type of music that originated in New Orleans, Louisiana in the early 20th century. It is often seen as the foundation of American popular music, and has had a significant influence on many genres such as blues, rock and roll, and hip hop. The distinctive characteristics of jazz include improvisation, syncopation, polyrhythms and melodic ornamentation. 

Jazz developed through a synthesis of African rhythms and European harmonies which were brought together by musicians in New Orleans who had roots in both cultures. From there it spread throughout the United States and beyond. Many great jazz musicians emerged in this period such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Charlie Parker and Billie Holiday who all made major contributions to the development of the genre. 

Jazz is often considered to be a democratic art form since it allows individual expression within the context of collective improvisation.
